steps: Biodiversity is the variety of living organisms found in an area or on Earth, including diversity within species, between species and among ecosystems.
Different organisms perform different roles in ecosystems, such as producers, consumers and decomposers.
Biodiversity helps maintain food chains and food webs, and supports processes such as pollination, decomposition and nutrient cycling.
A diverse ecosystem is generally more stable and better able to withstand environmental changes and disturbances.
Biodiversity also provides humans with useful resources, including food, medicines and raw materials.
items.finalAnswer: Biodiversity—the variety of life within and among species and ecosystems—supports ecosystem processes, stability and resilience.

steps: The Linnaean system classifies organisms into groups according to their similarities and differences.
It is a hierarchical system: each larger group contains one or more smaller groups.
The seven taxonomic ranks, from the broadest to the most specific, are Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus and Species.
A kingdom contains phyla; a phylum contains classes; a class contains orders; an order contains families; a family contains genera; and a genus contains species.
Species is the basic and most specific rank; organisms within a species share many characteristics and can usually interbreed to produce fertile offspring.
As we move from Kingdom towards Species, the groups become smaller and their organisms share more characteristics.
items.finalAnswer: The Linnaean hierarchy is Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species, with each increasingly specific rank grouping organisms that share more characteristics.

steps: The domain Eukarya contains organisms whose cells have a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
Kingdom Protista: mostly unicellular eukaryotes; some are autotrophic and others are heterotrophic.
Kingdom Fungi: eukaryotic organisms that obtain food by absorption; their cell walls contain chitin, and most are multicellular.
Kingdom Plantae: multicellular eukaryotes with cellulose cell walls and chloroplasts; most make food by photosynthesis.
Kingdom Animalia: multicellular eukaryotes without cell walls; they obtain food by ingestion and are usually capable of movement.
items.finalAnswer: The four Eukarya kingdoms are Protista (mostly unicellular), Fungi (absorptive heterotrophs with chitin cell walls), Plantae (photosynthetic organisms with cellulose cell walls) and Animalia (ingestive heterotrophs without cell walls).
